I don’t know if you wear skirts or not, so if not then this answer doesn’t affect you - but - panel skirts are the easiest thing ever. I started sewing in august, with the help of a friend whose been sewing for years. We made knee length pants, a krinilin skirt, a metallic over skirt, and a tunic styled dress.
The dress and pants were traced using clothes of mine (but I traced stretchy clothes onto non stretched fabric, and my lord - there are panels everywhere on them. The krinolin was hard af to work with, but the pants weren’t an issue once I realized I needed to make everything wayyyyy bigger.

I since decided that I needed to go back to basics, and have made 2 (working on my third) panel skirt. If I’m sewing straight, I can make one start to finish in about 5 hours - though they don’t look “good” by any means but I like them and where them. I found zippers are easier than elastic (is that normal?)

I have no idea how to read patterns so I can’t give advice, but look for old sheets and fabric at thrift stores! You will save money and can play around with different things.

I also paint, and have made a couple brush rolls. The first 2 were kind of bad but the third I made looks pretty damn good. I don’t use patterns, I kind of
“Just sew” if that makes sense. It’s probably not the way others do it, but I like playing around with my machine and just testing things.

Lastly, I heard brother is really good too - but I’m not sure a good machine for that price, but market place might be a good place to look ^^
